title: Altermagnetic Kondo Logic via Floquet Symmetry Conversion
authors: Haojie Shen, Xinchen Zhou, Baigeng Wang, Rui Wang
abstract: A common belief in Kondo physics is that a magnetic impurity can act as an efficient probe of key properties of its host bath. In altermagnets, however, this intuition fails in a symmetry-enforced way: the momentum-dependent spin splitting cancels in the local impurity spectrum, making a conventional single-impurity Kondo resonance essentially blind to the altermagnetic form factor. Here, we overcome this constraint by introducing Floquet symmetry conversion. We show that an in-plane AC field converts the hidden altermagnetic spin splitting into a locally detectable spin-dependent hybridization channel, which is further amplified by Kondo correlations into a novel altermagnetic Kondo effect. Remarkably, the Kondo splitting exhibits a nontrivial dependence on the field orientation and inherits the same crystalline form factor as the altermagnetic host, thereby serving as Kondo tomography of altermagnetic spin splitting. This field-controlled response further provides a natural route to symmetry-controlled Kondo logic gates. Our results establish a field-controllable altermagnetic Kondo effect, linking symmetry-resolved impurity spectroscopy to Kondo logic functionality.
summary: This work introduces a novel mechanism to probe the hidden spin structure of altermagnets using an external AC electric field. By employing Floquet symmetry conversion, the authors make the altermagnetic form factor visible to a local impurity, leading to a field-controlled Kondo effect. This effect is powerful because it allows the system to function as a controllable quantum logic gate (e.g., XOR or AND) based on the underlying crystal symmetry.
main_problem: Conventional Kondo resonance in altermagnets is blind to the host's momentum-dependent spin splitting due to symmetry cancellation in the local impurity spectrum.
main_result: Applying an in-plane AC field converts this hidden altermagnetic splitting into a locally detectable channel, realizing a field-controllable Kondo effect that acts as a symmetry-resolved probe and logic gate.
method: The authors use Floquet symmetry conversion theory combined with advanced impurity spectroscopy techniques like NRG to analyze the field-renormalized Kondo resonance.
model_or_system: The system involves a local impurity coupled to an altermagnetic host characterized by momentum-dependent spin splittings (e.g., $d$-wave or $g$-wave form factors). The physics is analyzed using the Anderson impurity model mapped onto a Wilson chain.
key_observables: The Kondo resonance splitting, spectral spin contrast ($P_A(\omega)$), and the resulting logic gate output state (split/unsplit resonance).
important_parameters: AC field amplitude ($a_0$), field orientation ($\phi$), and the ratio of the induced splitting to the Kondo temperature ($B_{ex}/T_K$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the leading high-frequency Floquet expansion and assumes the altermagnet has well-defined spin-resolved Fermi surfaces.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mechanism of field-induced coupling, the resulting Kondo splitting dependence on field orientation ($\phi$), and truth tables demonstrating the realization of XOR and AND logic gates using different altermagnetic symmetries ($B_{1g}, B_{2g}$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the blindness issue, then introduces Floquet conversion via an AC field, calculates the resulting Kondo splitting, and finally demonstrates its application in realizing specific, symmetry-controlled quantum logic gates (XOR, AND, XNOR).
why_interesting: The concept of using external fields to engineer spectroscopic signatures in strongly correlated materials is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum sensing, providing a pathway to read out otherwise hidden quantum information.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
